title: 卖旧衣服的 2nd Street，为什么在日本门店比优衣库还多？
title_en: Why Does Secondhand-Clothing Chain 2nd Street Have More Stores in Japan Than Uniqlo?
summary_cn: 声动早咖啡拆解日本二手服装连锁 2nd Street（Second Street）：日本门店超900家、全球超1000家，已超过优衣库日本门店数。核心逻辑是闲置经济土壤、母公司 GEO 的全国门店网络与人力买手定价体系三管齐下，把最难标准化的服装品类做成了规模化直营连锁
summary_en: This episode breaks down 2nd Street, the Japanese secondhand-clothing chain that runs over 900 stores across Japan and more than 1,000 worldwide, outpacing Uniqlo's Japan count. The winning formula combines three things: a country where the idle-economy soil is deep, parent company GEO's nationwide store network, and a human-buyer pricing system. Together they turned apparel — the hardest category to standardize — into a scale-model direct-operated chain that few rivals have matched.

scenes.title_cn: 轻解读：2nd Street 如何把二手服装做成千家连锁
scenes.title_en: Light Analysis: How 2nd Street Built a Thousand-Store Chain in Secondhand Apparel
scenes.context: 主播拆解 2nd Street 从收旧衣到千店直营的完整逻辑，并与优衣库、Goodwill 对比。语域：casual 播客讲解 + 商业分析。
scenes.speak: 2nd Street buys used clothes from consumers, processes them, and puts them back on shelves. As of March this year it had over nine hundred stores in Japan, covering all forty-seven prefectures, and more than one thousand worldwide, including the US, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia. The key insight: most Japanese secondhand players with over a thousand stores concentrate on easily standardized categories like gold, bags, and electronics, and rely heavily on franchising. 2nd Street does apparel in a direct-operated model, which is rare globally; its parent company ranks first in Japan's secondhand industry by revenue, seventy percent ahead of the runner-up. For comparison, North America's Goodwill has over three thousand stores, but it's a nonprofit whose inventory comes from donations. 2nd Street is a commercial buy-and-resell model. As the episode puts it, "It has opened more than nine hundred stores in Japan, while Uniqlo has fewer than eight hundred stores there." Yet despite more stores, its profit is less than a tenth of Uniqlo's. The deep soil behind it: rapid postwar economic growth created mass consumption and idle goods; when the economy slowed, people started selling them off. Japanese households hold idle items worth roughly ninety-one trillion yen — about five hundred seventy billion dollars — and fashion apparel makes up more than a third of that.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：2nd Street 从消费者手中收购旧衣，经处理后上架销售。截至今年 3 月，日本门店超 900 家，覆盖全部 47 个都道府县，全球（含美国、台湾、东南亚）超 1000 家
sentences.en: 2nd Street buys used clothes from consumers, processes them, and puts them back on shelves. As of March this year it had over 900 stores in Japan, covering all 47 prefectures, and more than 1,000 worldwide, including the US, Taiwan, and Southeast Asia.
sentences.note: 表达提示used clothes / secondhand clothing → 二手服装；prefecture → 都道府县；buy-and-resell → 收购再售

sentences.cn: 关键理解：日本二手行业过千店的玩家多集中在黄金、包袋、数码等易标准化品类，且大量采用加盟。2nd Street 以直营模式做服装，全球罕见；母公司在日本二手行业收入排名第一，比第二名高 70%
sentences.en: The key insight: most Japanese secondhand players with over a thousand stores focus on easily standardized categories like gold, bags, and electronics, and rely heavily on franchising. 2nd Street runs apparel in a direct-operated model — rare globally. Its parent company ranks first in Japan's secondhand industry by revenue, 70% ahead of the runner-up.
sentences.note: 表达提示easily standardized category → 易标准化品类；franchising → 加盟模式；direct-operated model → 直营模式；runner-up → 第二名

sentences.cn: 典型场景：北美 Goodwill 有 3000+ 店但是非营利组织、货源靠捐赠；2nd Street 是商业收购再售模式
sentences.en: A telling comparison: North America's Goodwill has 3,000-plus stores, but it's a nonprofit whose inventory comes from donations. 2nd Street, by contrast, runs a commercial buy-and-resell model.
sentences.note: 表达提示nonprofit → 非营利组织；inventory comes from donations → 货源靠捐赠；by contrast → 相比之下

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「在日本开出了 900 多家门店，而优衣库在日本的门店数量还不到 800 家」
sentences.en: "It has opened more than 900 stores in Japan, while Uniqlo has fewer than 800 stores there."
sentences.note: 表达提示open stores → 开出门店；fewer than → 不到（数量对比）

sentences.cn: （引用）相关概念：与优衣库对比——门店数已超过优衣库日本约 800 家，但利润不到优衣库十分之一
sentences.en: The comparison with Uniqlo: it now outnumbers Uniqlo's roughly 800 Japan stores, yet its profit is less than a tenth of Uniqlo's.
sentences.note: 表达提示outnumber → 数量超过；less than a tenth → 不到十分之一

sentences.cn: 二战后经济高速增长带来大量消费和闲置；经济下滑后居民开始出售旧货。日本家庭闲置超一年物品总值约 91 万亿日元（约 5700 亿美元），时尚服装占比超三分之一
sentences.en: Postwar rapid economic growth created mass consumption and piles of idle goods; when the economy slowed, households started selling their old stuff off. Japanese households hold idle items worth about 91 trillion yen — roughly 570 billion dollars — and fashion apparel makes up more than a third of that value.
sentences.note: 表达提示idle goods / idle economy → 闲置物品/闲置经济；sell sth off → 出售旧货；make up more than a third → 占比超三分之一

paraphrase.intent: 想说「门店数量超过优衣库」
phrases: It now has more stores in Japan than Uniqlo.
Its store count has outpaced Uniqlo's across the country.
paraphrase.chunks: more stores than · outpace · store count
paraphrase.usage: 口语用第一句直接对比，点评/文章用 outpace

paraphrase.intent: 想说「这家店是直营，不加盟」
phrases: It runs everything itself — no franchising.
The chain is fully direct-operated, which is rare in this category.
paraphrase.usage: 第一句口语，第二句更正式、适合分析

paraphrase.intent: 想说「利润远不如优衣库」
phrases: Its profit is a fraction of Uniqlo's.
Despite more stores, it earns less than a tenth of Uniqlo's profit.
paraphrase.chunks: a fraction of · less than a tenth
paraphrase.usage: a fraction of 简洁有力，具体数字时用第二句

scenes.title_cn: 快讯速览：本期其他商业科技动态
scenes.title_en: News Roundup: Other Business & Tech Moves This Week
scenes.context: 快速浏览本期其他快讯：火山引擎视频模型、茶百道咖啡、DeepMind 与 A24、TOTO 半导体材料。语域：casual 快讯播报。
scenes.speak: Volcano Engine announced that Seedance 2.5 will launch in early July. Its core feature is using 3D modeling for pre-visualization: simulating camera movement first to guarantee consistent shots, then rendering materials and lighting. Seedance 2.0 already changed China's short-drama industry, but a 4K 30-second clip of 2.5 costs over two hundred yuan, which sits awkwardly against the cost-driven short-drama market. So it fits commercial and professional filmmaking better than mass-produced micro-dramas chasing rock-bottom costs. Meanwhile, ChaPanda launched its first coffee collaboration with the animation "A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality," and its coffee footprint has grown from about two hundred stores early this year to over two thousand seven hundred. Milk-tea brands like Guming and Mixue are piling into coffee, using their supply chains and store networks to grab share. DeepMind invested seventy-five million dollars with A24 to build filmmaking AI tools, but won't access A24's library data; storyboard generation is becoming a hot AI use case in the industry, with the final work still human-led. And TOTO, the Japanese bathroom giant, plans to spend four hundred ninety-five million dollars over five years expanding into semiconductor materials, applying its ceramic-firing tech to electrostatic chucks that hold silicon wafers. That new business is only ten percent of revenue but already contributes over half of total profit, outpacing the core bathroom unit. Why it matters: GEO knew clothing appraisal relies on human experience and can't be standardized like books or games — yet precisely because those barriers mean less competition, it picked apparel, the largest category.

sentences.cn: 火山引擎宣布 7 月初发布 Seedance 2.5，核心能力是以 3D 建模做预演，先模拟镜头运动保证运镜一致性，再渲染材质光影。Seedance 2.0 已改变中国短剧行业，但 2.5 的 4K 30 秒成本超 200 元，与低成本短剧需求有落差
sentences.en: Volcano Engine announced Seedance 2.5 for early July. Its core feature is 3D-modeling pre-visualization: simulating camera movement first to guarantee consistent shots, then rendering materials and lighting. Seedance 2.0 already transformed China's short-drama industry, but a 4K 30-second clip of 2.5 costs over 200 yuan, which sits awkwardly against the low-cost short-drama demand.
sentences.note: 表达提示pre-visualization → 预演；consistent shots → 运镜一致性；short drama → 短剧；sit awkwardly against → 与…有落差

sentences.cn: （引用）适用边界：更适合商用和专业影视创作，而非追求极致低成本的短剧量产
sentences.en: Its boundary: it suits commercial and professional filmmaking better than mass-producing micro-dramas that chase rock-bottom costs.
sentences.note: 表达提示boundary / applicability → 适用边界；micro-drama → 短剧；rock-bottom cost → 极致低成本

sentences.cn: 茶百道与《凡人修仙传》合作推出首个咖啡联名，咖啡覆盖门店从年初约 200 家增至超 2700 家。古茗、蜜雪冰城等新茶饮品牌集体做咖啡，利用供应链和门店网络争夺咖啡市场
sentences.en: ChaPanda launched its first coffee collaboration with "A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality," and stores offering coffee grew from about 200 early this year to over 2,700. Milk-tea brands like Guming and Mixue are piling into coffee, using their supply chains and store networks to grab a share of the market.
sentences.note: 表达提示collaboration / co-branding → 联名；milk-tea brand → 新茶饮品牌；pile into → 集体涌入；grab a share → 争夺市场份额

sentences.cn: DeepMind 投资 7500 万美元与 A24 共同开发电影制作 AI 工具，但不访问 A24 片库数据。分镜生成成为影视行业热门 AI 场景，确保最终作品仍由人类主导
sentences.en: DeepMind invested $75 million with A24 to jointly develop filmmaking AI tools, but won't access A24's library data. Storyboard generation is becoming a hot AI use case in film, with the final work still human-led.
sentences.note: 表达提示filmmaking AI tools → 电影制作 AI 工具；storyboard → 分镜；human-led → 由人类主导

sentences.cn: 日本卫浴巨头 TOTO 计划 5 年投资 4.95 亿美元扩展半导体材料业务，将陶瓷烧制技术用于静电吸盘（固定硅晶圆）。新业务仅占营收 10%，但贡献利润已超总利润一半，超过核心卫浴业务
sentences.en: Japanese bathroom giant TOTO plans to invest $495 million over five years to expand its semiconductor-materials business, applying its ceramic-firing technology to electrostatic chucks that hold silicon wafers. The new business is only 10% of revenue but already contributes more than half of total profit, surpassing its core bathroom unit.
sentences.note: 表达提示electrostatic chuck → 静电吸盘；silicon wafer → 硅晶圆；ceramic firing → 陶瓷烧制；surpass → 超过

sentences.cn: 为什么重要：GEO 明知服装鉴定依赖人的经验、无法像书籍游戏那样标准化，却正因为这些门槛让竞争更少，选择了服饰这个最大品类
sentences.en: Why it matters: GEO knew clothing appraisal depends on human experience and can't be standardized the way books or games can — yet precisely because those barriers mean less competition, it chose apparel, the largest category.
sentences.note: 表达提示appraisal → 鉴定/估价；standardize → 标准化；barriers → 门槛；the largest category → 最大品类

paraphrase.intent: 想说「成本太高，跟短剧市场对不上」
phrases: The cost is out of step with what micro-dramas can pay.
Pricing that high just doesn't fit the short-drama economics.
paraphrase.chunks: out of step with · short-drama economics
paraphrase.usage: out of step with 偏书面，第二句更口语直白

paraphrase.intent: 想说「品牌们都在做咖啡」
phrases: Every milk-tea brand is piling into coffee now.
Coffee is suddenly everyone's second act.
paraphrase.usage: pile into 口语描述趋势；second act 是俏皮的评论说法

phrases: The new line already earns more than the core business.
It contributes over half of total profit despite being a fraction of revenue.
paraphrase.chunks: earn more than · a fraction of revenue
paraphrase.usage: 第一句口语对比，第二句适合带数据的分析

practice.cn: 用「outpace」说：2nd Street 门店数已超过优衣库。
practice.en: 2nd Street has outpaced Uniqlo's Japan store count.

practice.cn: 用「franchising」说：这家店全是直营，不加盟。
practice.en: It's fully direct-operated — no franchising at all.

practice.cn: 用「pile into」说：新茶饮品牌都在做咖啡。
practice.en: Milk-tea brands are piling into coffee with their supply chains.

practice.cn: 用「a fraction of」说：利润不到优衣库的十分之一。
practice.en: Its profit is only a fraction of Uniqlo's.

pitfalls.wrong: The store is very many, more than Uniqlo.
pitfalls.right: It has more stores in Japan than Uniqlo does.
pitfalls.why: 中文式「很很多」直译不成立；英文用 more … than 比较结构，或动词 outnumber / outpace。

pitfalls.wrong: They buy second-hand clothes from consumers and sell them.
pitfalls.right: It buys used clothes from consumers, processes them, and resells them.
pitfalls.why: 作为商业流程描述，补上 processing 环节信息更完整；resell 比重复 sell 更地道。

pitfalls.wrong: The clothing is very hard to standardize.
pitfalls.right: Apparel is one of the hardest categories to standardize.
pitfalls.why: 直译「服装很难标准化」缺少对比语境；用 one of the hardest categories 表达相对难度更贴切。

pitfalls.wrong: GEO knows appraisal needs people, but still chooses clothes.
pitfalls.right: GEO knew appraisal depends on human experience, yet chose apparel precisely because those barriers mean less competition.
pitfalls.why: 只译「需要人」丢掉了关键的「门槛高所以竞争少」因果逻辑；要补上理由才能表达原意。

shifts.before: 以为二手服装店是低端、难规模化的生意
shifts.after: 直营+买手定价+全国网络，能让最难标准化的服装做成千家连锁

shifts.before: 以为门店多就等于利润高
shifts.after: 门店数超过优衣库，利润却不到其十分之一——规模不等于盈利

shifts.before: 以为标准化是规模化的唯一前提
shifts.after: 高门槛品类反而竞争更少，GEO 故意选最难做的服饰品类
